Top News
 
 
 
 Meta, Tesla, SpaceX earnings 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
 Wall Street heads into a heavy earnings week, with Meta Platforms and Tesla among the biggest names set to report as investors look for fresh reads on AI spending, advertising demand and consumer resilience.

 Meta Platforms ( META ) and Tesla ( TSLA ) report Wednesday, alongside Lam Research ( LRCX ) and Texas Instruments ( TXN ). The reports will put both the AI trade and the broader semiconductor complex back in focus.

 The earnings rush begins Tuesday with SpaceX ( SPCX ), Netflix ( NFLX ), GE Aerospace ( GE ), RTX ( RTX ), General Motors ( GM ) and United Airlines ( UAL ). SpaceX’s report should draw particular attention as investors assess growth, margins and spending following its blockbuster debut. Nvidia ( NVDA ) will also hold its GTC Berlin AI conference, with CEO Jensen Huang scheduled to speak.

Thursday brings another broad slate, including Spotify ( SPOT ), Procter & Gamble ( PG ), Lockheed Martin ( LMT ), Honeywell ( HON ), American Airlines ( AAL ) and Comcast ( CMCSA ).

 Elsewhere, Kroger ( KR ) holds an investor day Tuesday, while the Federal Reserve enters its blackout period ahead of the Oct. 27-28 policy meeting. Monday also marks the 39th anniversary of the 1987 Black Monday crash.

 Investing Group Spotlight 
 
 
Banking stocks have come under pressure as Bank of America tempers expectations for Q3, creating potential opportunities for investors. In his latest article, The Investment Doctor examines BAC’s earnings outlook, financial strength, and credit quality while highlighting why its Series L preferred shares may be attractive again. His analysis explores the potential for dividend income and capital gains as market conditions evolve.

( Free Full Article ) Here’s a brief summary of the article:

Bank of America ( BAC ) delivered strong Q2 results, but management has tempered expectations for Q3, citing a less favorable global markets environment. The bank’s shares have declined significantly alongside the broader financial sector, bringing its forward P/E ratio to approximately 10.5. Investors will monitor loan delinquencies and non-performing assets for signs of deteriorating credit quality, although BAC’s strong balance sheet and CET1 capital ratio above regulatory minimums provide a solid buffer against potential challenges.

The bank’s Series L preferred shares have also become attractive again. These “busted” preferred shares can be converted into common stock if BAC’s share price exceeds $65 for 20 days within a 30-day period. With the common stock pulling back, conversion risk has diminished, pushing preferred share prices lower. At current levels, Series L offers a dividend yield of approximately 6.06%, alongside potential capital appreciation if BAC shares recover toward the conversion threshold.

Despite near-term uncertainties, BAC’s underlying performance remains strong, and preferred dividend obligations represent only a small portion of net income. The author sees opportunities in both common and preferred shares, combining potential capital gains with dividend income.
